System

Consumables, tools and item-use effects

Item use validates an owned consumable/tool and applies its authored effect under one replay-safe operation. Consuming a potion must not grant healing twice on a repeated packet, and a rejected use must not remove the item.

Scope and player interaction

Item use validates an owned consumable/tool and applies its authored effect under one replay-safe operation. Consuming a potion must not grant healing twice on a repeated packet, and a rejected use must not remove the item.

StageMeaning
First integration: Phase09committed; full feature contract may include explicitly staged later extensions
EvidenceAuthored implementation specification; no native/Blueprint/backend runtime verified

UI state machine

Ready → UsePending → EffectAccepted → Cooldown → Rejected

WBP_ActionBar observes results from URPGItemUseComponent. Pending is not Accepted. Close/cancel clears local focus and stale callbacks, but cannot undo an already committed backend command.

Definitions, fields and units

Canonical definition: DA_Item_HealingDraught. Stable IDs, quantities, seconds and centimeters are validated by the owner, not inferred from translated labels or sprites.

Field / rule
UseDefinitionId: allowed effect, target policy, cooldown tag and consumption policy
OwnedItemReference: instance UUID or versioned stack identity
UseExecutionId/CommandId: persistent receipt for consumption; bounded live effect deduplication
ToolCategory: Pickaxe|Axe|FishingRod|CraftTool; profession requirements separate
DurabilityCost: integer policy, committed once at terminal action
UseContext: session epoch and approved target; no client-provided heal amount

C++ / Blueprint / backend ownership

LayerResponsibility
URPGItemUseComponentImplement the native validated request/state lifecycle described below; native runtime state is not editable by UMG.
Blueprint/Data AssetsTune the declared defaults and visual/asset assignments. Keep definition references EditDefaultsOnly/BlueprintReadOnly; cosmetic hooks cannot grant rewards.
Zone serverValidate live actor ownership, range/LOS, alive/action state, cooldown/tool/target rules and current session epoch where relevant.
BackendFor durable changes, revalidate trusted catalog/revision/ownership and commit records/source claims/receipt atomically. Read-only/cosmetic features have no durable mutation.
WBP_ActionBarLocal observer/requester. Create only for local player; bind once, refresh immediately, unbind on teardown.

Custom command contracts

These names are project custom APIs or backend proposals, not existing Unreal/PaperZD nodes. Economic/backend requests are asynchronous; Pending resolves through the same command ID. Pure local queries are synchronous unless noted.

Command / result
RequestUseItem(CommandId, OwnedReference, TargetIntent) -> Accepted|ItemMissing|Cooldown|TargetInvalid
CommitConsumableUse(ValidatedContext) -> UseReceipt|Rejected; backend
ApplyAcceptedItemEffect(UseReceipt, AvatarLifeId) -> Applied|AlreadyApplied|RecoveryPolicy; server

End-to-end command and observation flow

  1. Player activates a hotbar item reference; server resolves actual ownership and use definition, validates target/alive state/cooldown and reserves the action.
  2. Backend atomically consumes the stack quantity or durability and records a use entitlement/receipt with the accepted effect parameters.
  3. Zone applies the live effect once using receipt ID and current avatar-life binding; never let a replayed receipt heal a later respawned body again.
  4. To close a crash gap, persist the chosen consumable recovery policy: on uncertain effect application during zone crash, restore the durable post-use resource snapshot or reconcile entitlement before enabling the next avatar. Do not simply consume in SQL then forget the effect.
  5. Publish owner inventory/resource updates and cosmetic cue from the accepted result. A non-economic gather tool check does not itself consume a tool unless the action's terminal policy says so.
  6. On transfer, drain/reconcile item-use commands before snapshot; long cooldown expiry follows the durable cooldown policy.

Editor configuration and real consumers

  1. Author DA_Item_HealingDraught with an allowed heal effect and shared item cooldown. Assign it to a versioned action-bar slot reference, not a fixed bag index.
  2. Add URPGItemUseComponent to PlayerState/controller-authorized command route and bind WBP_ActionBar use controls.
  3. Seed Character_A at 40/100 health with two draughts; use a proposed 30-health effect for a concrete expected result of 70 health and one remaining item.
  4. Reopen persistence schema to include the consumable entitlement/resource-snapshot recovery rule and add crash-between-consume-and-effect fixture.
  5. Reopen gathering/fishing/crafting tool checks to query equipment/inventory tool categories with the same item requirements; cosmetics do not establish tool ownership.

Reopen Phase09 integration entries after creating the assets. Test fixture: L_Rillmere / PotionStack_A / Character_A at 40 health. No later-phase runtime dependency should be activated before its recorded integration phase.

Failure, contention and recovery acceptance

Test stimulus and expected result
Same use packet twice -> one item consumed and one 30-health application.
Potion missing or stack replaced -> ItemMissing/StaleItem, no heal.
Use while dead -> TargetInvalid before commit.
Crash after consumption before live effect -> explicit entitlement/resource recovery, not silent loss or duplicate heal.

Repeat the success route with two clients when networking exists, then disconnect immediately before/after a committed result. Query the same command and compare authoritative snapshot/receipt with UI. Restart the relevant zone, reject stale epochs, and rerun the previous phase route. Pure visual/input features instead verify cleanup and unchanged server facts. These are future test recipes, not reported passes.

Tuning, accessibility and observability

Training potion heals 30 and uses a 10-second item cooldown; tune later. No client economy prediction. Tool durability cost is initially zero unless the terminal action definition explicitly enables it.

Log receipt/effect application linkage and recovery outcomes. Hotbar tooltips show count/cooldown and keyboard/controller prompts; rejected uses have readable text.

Art gaps, production and do-not-build-yet

The asset ZIP and installed PaperZD APIs remain unverified. Required new art/unsupported layer combinations are tracked in art/animation-matrix.html and art/equipment-visual-matrix.html. A legal debug visual can prove authority but is not finished content. Production features listed as later/optional remain disabled until their phase/gate passes.
